subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose model-facing browser network inspection/interception, and should the first supported contract be passive redacted diagnostics or active request interception?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API controls sensitive authenticated browser traffic and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Ship Passive Redacted Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body retrieval through the browser tool with redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before considering active interception.

options.title: Allow Active Interception With Policy
options.body: Add request interception or mutation only after maintainers define permissions, opt-in behavior, profile limits, and security review requirements.

options.title: Keep It Off The Model Surface
options.body: Leave network inspection on lower control/CLI surfaces or external workflows if model-facing access is judged too risky.

recommendation.title: Ship Passive Redacted Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body retrieval through the browser tool with redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before considering active interception.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest browser tool schema/runtime and browser route history for this product/security decision.
